q: The queen's speech had a profound ___ on everyone.
explain: have an impact on. ('affect' is a verb.)

q: After months of practice, her efforts finally paid ___.
The evidence was ___; nobody could argue with it.
We need to ___ the pros and cons before deciding.
He's ___ to win — he's the best by far.
explain: be bound to = be certain to.

q: Swimming is ___ prohibited in the north lake.
The new rules will come into ___ next month.
explain: come into force = start to apply (laws/rules).

q: She ___ out of the competition due to injury.
I can't ___ the difference between the two crystals.
The manager ___ the blame for the mistake.
There has been a sharp ___ in the number of visitors.
explain: a rise (noun) in numbers; 'raise' is mainly a verb.

q: He has a reputation ___ being honest.
Her explanation was ___; I understood instantly.
explain: crystal clear = very easy to understand.

q: We managed to ___ the problem by working together.
explain: overcome a problem = deal with it successfully.

q: He's very ___; he always finishes what he starts.
Which word is the opposite of 'reluctant'?
explain: Reluctant = not wanting to; willing = happy to.
